review_scope: Registered-source content review of Plugin estimation of smooth optimal transport maps by Tudor Manole, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Jonathan Niles-Weed and Larry Wasserman. The registered 99-page file prints arXiv:2107.12364v3 and 16 June 2024. Main text ends above y=637.536865234375 on shared PDF page 29. Fresh extraction and the rendered page stop at that boundary; a separate crop contains only the Appendix A heading. No appendix body or later reference pages were read.
inventory: Exactly nine Theorems occur in the main-text region: 1 on page 9, 3 on 10, 5 on 11, 6 on 12, 10 on 16, 18 on 21-22, 20 on 24, 22 on 26 and 24 on 28. Background Theorems 1,3,5 remain included. The inventory excludes contents/proof references, ordinary mentions, Lemmas, Propositions and Corollaries. Every complete statement and all subparts were compared with rendered pages.
original_statements: Theorem 1 preserves the distinct assumptions on P and Q, finite-valued global convex potential, semi-dual reference, uniqueness qualifications and literal Lebesgue-almost-everywhere inverse identities. The conjugate gradient and the forward gradient are not interchanged.

Theorem 3 preserves S1, density bounds, uniqueness up to a constant, both noninteger-alpha requirements, the closure of the interior subdomain, all constant dependencies and the different interior/global conclusions. Theorem 5 preserves the torus density assumptions and cube norm for the convex lift, without adding an unprinted potential normalization or noninteger restriction.

Theorem 6 preserves its deterministic arbitrary-target formulation, population curvature condition, both inequalities, squared map loss and the subtracted integral of the target Kantorovich potential. No sampling or estimated-density regularity hypothesis is added.

Theorem 10 preserves the complete wavelet result: tuning, positive target-density ball, curvature only in part (i), conjugate-potential ball and source-density bounds in part (ii), all dimension-dependent rates including log(n)^2/n in dimension two, bias bound and squared-error bound with its variance term.

Theorem 18 includes its page-22 continuation, smoothness/kernel/tuning hypotheses, every rate including log(n)/n in dimension two, noninteger-alpha restriction only in part (ii), bias and squared-error bounds with both variances under one square root.

Theorem 20 preserves C1, constrained densities, noninteger alpha, L_n^(1/d) tuning, cutoff dependence, the barred one-sample map with its potential regularity assumption, and the hatted two-sample map under C2. The final comma is literal; following prose and the footnote are excluded from the statement.

Theorem 22 preserves all three branches and references (38)-(39), the smoothness/dimension thresholds, extra hypercube potential assumptions and extra conjugate condition for its two-sample assertion. The referenced Gaussian limits, variance mixture and preceding tuning conventions are archived separately. No nonzero-variance or P-not-equal-Q assumption is inserted.

Theorem 24 preserves all three barred constants and the bound on local parameters, suprema over finite sets, arbitrary estimator sequences, exact scaled alternatives, product-law expectations, both risk bounds and endpoint sample-size ratios. The paths are the particular source-referenced paths; no guessed formula replaces their excluded construction.
source_passages: All 40 source entries and 17 auxiliary excerpts were checked. The Euclidean support condition, probability/absolute-continuity notation, measurable transport maps, couplings, squared cost, dual feasibility and semi-dual/conjugation conventions agree with pages 3 and 8-9. The printed L1(Omega) dual convention and solves-to wording remain literal.

The induced population Brenier map and Kantorovich potentials retain the distinction between curly varphi and straight phi. Hölder notation on page 7 explicitly defers its exact norm to Appendix A; norm-only and positive balls are distinct and neither silently adds density normalization.

Torus metric, periodic unit-cell measures, Monge problem, cost and dual match pages 10-11. The source switch of potential glyph in the feasibility clause is preserved. The convex lift and its periodic quadratic correction remain distinct. Proposition 4 supplies auxiliary conventions, with its skipped item (iv) left unchanged; it is not added to the theorem inventory.

The one-sample experiment, deterministic curvature condition, empirical measure, boundary-corrected wavelet families, empirical coefficients, clipping/normalization and plugin map match pages 11-16. The level-j0 index bound and full-basis-versus-truncation equality are retained as printed. Wavelet construction details remain excluded rather than invented.

The torus two-sample setting, independent observations, population lift, induced potentials, kernel convolution, clipping/normalization, K1 Fourier condition and estimated map agree with pages 20-21. The risk uses Euclidean differences of chosen lifts. Kernel construction and Fourier-order regularity remain separate; kernel nonnegativity is not added.

Smooth-domain C1/C2, local observations, mean-zero Neumann operator domain and eigenbasis, separate constant-one density component, smooth cutoff, weighted series, normalized measures and both maps match pages 23-24. The target series uses the same printed omega_l indexed through L_n. Constrained Hölder densities are not mean-zero functions. C2 remains an assumption whose general-domain validity the source leaves open.

The central-limit preamble and equations (38)-(39) preserve tuning, sample independence, variance mixture and population centering. The fixed-target cost functional, centered potential scores and explicit Appendix L path reference match pages 27-28. Smoothness, map and cost specializations use their actual domains.
dependency_review: All 62 direct uses and 109 related connections were checked against all 40 local definitions. Theorem 6 remains deterministic. The one-sample wavelet theorem uses the boundary-corrected estimator and its own sampling model. Theorem 18 uses the torus kernel estimator without importing population curvature as an extra hypothesis. Theorem 20 uses C1 and the spectral estimator; it does not acquire S1, torus restrictions, kernel estimators or K1 merely by reusing R_K notation. C2 belongs only to its two-sample branch. Theorem 22 retains the union of its three distinct branches and their actual limits. Theorem 24 specializes the cost functional to the torus and does not acquire the unused Euclidean branch or density-estimator dependencies. Named proof results and broader prose extensions are not imported as statement requirements.
names_and_highlights: All titles retain source-derived natural-language terms, and every entry has source-backed selectors checked against its own passage/label or a related theorem. Same notation on different domains does not merge Euclidean and torus definitions. Source passages, definitions and conditions remain distinct. D25 and D38 explicitly record specializations rather than presenting synthesized original definitions. All relationship explanations identify the actual local dependency path.

The main-text-only census is complete as an extraction and review; it does not claim to provide these missing constructions.
